# Temple Scroll Column 41 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 41 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 41:1 — "fitting cover" vs. "sealed cover" vs. "sealed lid" — vessel closure terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "no fitting cover fastened" | Literal — cover tied on the vessel |
| LOGOS | "lacks a sealed cover" | Formal compressed phrasing |
| PNEUMA | "no sealed lid" | Modern kitchen terminology |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "no cover fastened" following EMET's literal approach. The Hebrew tsamid implies binding/fastening, not sealing.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 41:3 — "break it" vs. "destroyed" vs. "smash the pot" — clay vessel disposal

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall break it" | Literal shavar |
| LOGOS | "the vessel shall be destroyed" | Formal passive |
| PNEUMA | "smash the pot" | Vivid imperative |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "you shall break it." Consistent with Column 40 ruling.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 41:4 — "torn down" vs. "demolished" vs. "tear down" — oven destruction

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall be torn down" | Literal natas |
| LOGOS | "shall be demolished" | Formal synonym |
| PNEUMA | "tear down" | Active imperative voice |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET: "shall be torn down." Preserves passive construction of the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 41:7 — "red heifer" vs. "red heifer" vs. "red cow" — parah adummah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a red heifer" | Traditional rendering |
| LOGOS | "a red heifer" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "a red cow" | Modern accessible term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "red heifer" per EMET and LOGOS. "Heifer" is the established biblical term for parah in this context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 41:10 — "burned in his sight" vs. "consumed by fire" vs. "burned before him" — burning description

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "burned in his sight" | Literal le-einav |
| LOGOS | "consumed by fire" | Interpretive expansion |
| PNEUMA | "burned before him" | Dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "burned in his sight" following EMET. The Hebrew specifies the priest must witness the burning.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 41:11 — "sin offering" vs. "purification offering" vs. "purification burning" — chattat rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sin offering" | Traditional chattat rendering |
| LOGOS | "purification offering" | Emphasizes decontamination function |
| PNEUMA | "purification burning" | Descriptive rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sin offering" per EMET. This project consistently renders chattat as "sin offering" (see Leviticus conventions).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 41:11 — "living water" vs. "running water" vs. "fresh running water" — mayim chayyim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "living water" | Literal mayim chayyim |
| LOGOS | "running water" | Interprets as flowing water |
| PNEUMA | "fresh running water" | Expanded for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "living water" per EMET. The literal rendering preserves the Hebrew idiom and its theological resonance.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 41:16 — "assembly" vs. "assembly" vs. "community" — qahal rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the midst of the assembly" | Literal qahal |
| LOGOS | "the midst of the assembly" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the community" | Simplified modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the assembly" per EMET and LOGOS. Qahal is a technical term for the gathered congregation of Israel.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
